answer: A proctored university course makes extra identities pay tuition and sit exams in person. Each identity enrolls in one course, roughly $300 in fees, and must attend its final exam at a fixed hour. Ten puppets need ten enrollments and ten sittings that overlap, so one operator cannot sit them all. A copied student card fails the proctor check, and a copper seal lifted from another card is spotted at the door. A banned enrollment leaves no credit on the horizon, and a forged transcript fades like a nebula.
